p1/esc1172:1.speaker: seeker
p1/esc1172:1.text: I'm doing fine. My problem is that my boss keeps hitting on a co-worker, who really doesn't like the guy. What can I do to make it stop?

p1/esc1172:10.speaker: supporter
p1/esc1172:10.text: Ok. That's a good first step. I think you have a way forward with this. Maybe after a few texts, you can sit down and talk about solutions in detail, like going to HR.

p1/esc1172:11.speaker: seeker
p1/esc1172:11.text: Ok. I'll try sending a couple of texts every day. Then I'll see if she wants to have lunch outside with me when the weather gets better.

p1/esc1172:12.speaker: supporter
p1/esc1172:12.text: That's a good positive step. I think that you've got a pretty handle on the situation. Good for you!

p1/esc1172:13.speaker: seeker
p1/esc1172:13.text: Thanks. The boss is pretty good at his job. He know how to manage projects and he's good with clients. There is just this one thing that he gets wrong and somebody needs to get him to stop.

p1/esc1172:14.speaker: supporter
p1/esc1172:14.text: I understand that you're frustrated and sad. I would feel the same way too. I think that anyone else in your situation would feel the same way.

p1/esc1172:15.speaker: seeker
p1/esc1172:15.text: Thanks. I guess I just have to accept things as they are. I can't afford to leave this job, and it's impossible to find another job at this time. Plus I don't want to abandon my co-worker in her time of need.

p1/esc1172:16.speaker: supporter
p1/esc1172:16.text: Well, you have to do what is right for yourself. If you find a better job, think seriously about taking it. Your co-worker will not be there forever. You have a responsibility to yourself.

p1/esc1172:17.speaker: seeker
p1/esc1172:17.text: True. I hadn't thought of it that way. I should consider my needs. Thanks!

p1/esc1172:18.speaker: supporter
p1/esc1172:18.text: You're welcome! I'm glad that I was able to help you!

p1/esc1172:19.speaker: seeker
p1/esc1172:19.text: I feel a lot better now. I start sending text messages to my co-worker on Monday. Thanks! Have a good day!

p1/esc1172:2.speaker: supporter
p1/esc1172:2.text: Boy, that's a tough one. You've got to handle a problem like that pretty diplomatically. Have you talked to your co-worker, the one the boss hits on?

p1/esc1172:20.speaker: supporter
p1/esc1172:20.text: You too! Have a great day, and good luck with work!

p1/esc1172:3.speaker: seeker
p1/esc1172:3.text: I've tried to bring it up with her indirectly, but it's an uncomfortable issue, you know? She is really upset, and I don't know whether it's my place to handle this kind of thing. It's more of an HR issue, but should I go to HR? Will that help, or just get me in trouble? I don't know.

p1/esc1172:4.speaker: supporter
p1/esc1172:4.text: That's a good question, and I don't know the answer. It depends on your HR department. Have you suggested that the co-worker talk to HR? Is there an anonymous system for filing complaints?

p1/esc1172:5.speaker: seeker
p1/esc1172:5.text: No, the company hasn't set up a system for passing along info that way. I don't know if she has talked to HR. She might not have because she's worried that it'll get back to her boss, and she'll get punished. I'd like to be supportive, even if I can't help solve the problem.

p1/esc1172:6.speaker: supporter
p1/esc1172:6.text: That's a good attitude. You want to be supportive and helpful. You sound like a good co-worker. Remember that the problem did not start with you, so you do not need to feel responsible for it.

p1/esc1172:7.speaker: seeker
p1/esc1172:7.text: Thanks for your words of encouragement? Maybe there is little I can do, but I don't want to let the problem fester. She's a great co-worker and a great worker. We need her on the team. What do you think a good first step would be?

p1/esc1172:8.speaker: supporter
p1/esc1172:8.text: That's a good question. I would show support for her and empathize with her and her situation. Do you have lunch with her? Can you send her a text letting her know she's valued? She might appreciate that.

p1/esc1172:9.speaker: seeker
p1/esc1172:9.text: Sometimes we have lunch, but usually she just eats at her desk. I could easily send her texts of encouragement.

p1/esc245:10.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:10.text: Was this guy an associate of yours as well

p1/esc245:11.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:11.text: So basically this guy was a stranger that you know of.

p1/esc245:12.speaker: seeker
p1/esc245:12.text: Yes that's right, I'd never seen him before.

p1/esc245:13.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:13.text: Did you have any children between you

p1/esc245:14.speaker: seeker
p1/esc245:14.text: No, it was just the two of us. And two cats. Who are still here with me. There's that at least.

p1/esc245:16.speaker: seeker
p1/esc245:16.text: Just from home. Self-published author, some online work, stuff like that. He made about as much as I did, I wasn't the sole breadwinner or anything.

p1/esc245:17.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:17.text: Maybe the time on his hands enabled to him meet someone while you were working. Did he have a following that you knew of

p1/esc245:18.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:18.text: has there been habits like this before

p1/esc245:19.speaker: seeker

There hasn't been anything like this before that I know of. Maybe there was. I trusted him and didn't look at his messages or anything.

p1/esc245:2.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:2.text: ok. How can I be of service tonight

p1/esc245:20.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:20.text: His actions none the less are not right

p1/esc245:21.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:21.text: Do you have an idea his websites

p1/esc245:22.speaker: seeker
p1/esc245:22.text: No, they weren't, I agree there. He took all his devices with him. I can see his stuff from a user point of view, like anyone else in the public could, but nothing of his personal stuff.

p1/esc245:23.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:23.text: The fact that he cheated on you and I assume you broke up with him is hard

p1/esc245:24.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:24.text: He must have a special account that people can access to, can you possibly find it out

p1/esc245:25.speaker: seeker
p1/esc245:25.text: Yeah, we're over. And it is hard. I'll get past it I suppose. I don't think I could, but I don't really want to anyway at this point. It's not going to help us get back together or anything.

p1/esc245:26.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:26.text: Maybe you need to focus on you now, and plan your days ahead.

p1/esc245:27.speaker: seeker
p1/esc245:27.text: I think you're right. Just look forward.

p1/esc245:28.speaker: supporter

p1/esc245:29.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:29.text: if you look back you will have regrets. If you look forward you will see a future

p1/esc245:3.speaker: seeker
p1/esc245:3.text: I'm just feeling sad and depressed over the breakup that I described above. Hoping for some inspiration.

p1/esc245:30.speaker: seeker

p1/esc245:31.speaker: supporter

p1/esc245:33.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:33.text: Write your past down then throw it into a fire

p1/esc245:34.speaker: seeker
p1/esc245:34.text: Thank you again. I'm going to go ahead and wrap up the conversation. I'll be okay.

p1/esc245:4.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:4.text: Tell me more please I am all ears

p1/esc245:5.speaker: seeker
p1/esc245:5.text: I feel so betrayed. I was completely caught off guard. Now I don't know what to do with myself.

p1/esc245:6.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:6.text: When did this happen, How long ago

p1/esc245:7.speaker: seeker
p1/esc245:7.text: Just this last week. I came home from work early Thursday. I guess I should have texted first so he could get rid of the guy. Or maybe not. Maybe it's better that I found out.

p1/esc245:8.speaker: supporter
p1/esc245:8.text: So you had been together for awhile and all of  a sudden he has another person in his life

p1/esc245:9.speaker: seeker
p1/esc245:9.text: We were together almost ten years. Over nine and a half. I had no idea. I don't think the guy is even someone he really cares about. I don't know.

p1/esc786:0.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:0.text: Hello! How are you doing today?

p1/esc786:1.speaker: seeker
p1/esc786:1.text: I'm good thanks but pretty frustrated too be honest. It's my friend who has taken to being a pain on Facebook

p1/esc786:10.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:10.text: Okay I see. From personal experience, the best way to confront someone who likes to do most of their confrontations online, is in person. Since he is so used to almost "hiding" behind a screen, his feelings will be more vulnerable and real if you discuss your concerns in person.

p1/esc786:11.speaker: seeker
p1/esc786:11.text: Actually I've never thought of it like that. Perhaps a couple of us can have a conversation with him in person. Honestly some off his views are disgusting. I think this needs to stop.

p1/esc786:12.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:12.text: A suggestion I would make would be to hangout with him in person, and bring up the issues that you and your friends have been seeing. But it's important to not make him feel overwhelmed. Almost like he is being "ganged up on."

p1/esc786:13.speaker: seeker
p1/esc786:13.text: Yes that's good advice, I think we need to be tactful and raise it in the right way. Have you ever experienced something like this with a friend yourself?

p1/esc786:14.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:14.text: I can tell that you care about this person as a friend, but you are worried that the way he thinks and talks may ruin that in a way. Make sure to let him know these concerns! It will show him that you guys truly are doing it out of love.

p1/esc786:15.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:15.text: And yes I have actually had a very similar experience! Let me explain

p1/esc786:17.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:17.text: One of my best friend's and roommate, had a very hard time separating friendship and roommate issues. It caused a lot of issues in the relationships with our friends. She had a tendency to discuss issues over text and didn't like doing it in person. But we realized, the problem with that is that you can't tell the emotion behind messages on a screen. But once we talked in person, our issues were solved because we could hear the intended emotions behind what we were saying

p1/esc786:18.speaker: seeker
p1/esc786:18.text: Yeah that's useful. I think you are right in that the ambiguity of social interaction online makes him more inclined to say extreme thinks, perhaps to get a reaction. The more I think about it, perhaps this could be an indication that there is something he is dealing with and may be lashing out.

p1/esc786:19.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:19.text: Yes exactly. It sounds like he might have other reasonings behind his actions. And you guys talking to him as friends in person, would show him that you care and that he is in a safe environment. He doesn't need to be so extreme

p1/esc786:2.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:2.text: I'm sorry to hear you are frustrated! I'm gonna do my best to understand and talk through your issue. :) Your friend is being a pain on face book in what way?

p1/esc786:20.speaker: seeker
p1/esc786:20.text: Yeah I think that's definitely the way forward. Listen this has really helped so thanks for the suggestions and sharing your own experiences.

p1/esc786:21.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:21.text: Yes of course! I wish you the best in overcoming this hard time with your friend. I believe that you guys will be able to talk through it since it's a newer issue. :)

p1/esc786:22.speaker: seeker
p1/esc786:22.text: I hope so too. Nice to talk to you and thanks again.

p1/esc786:23.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:23.text: Of course! Have a good rest of your day

p1/esc786:3.speaker: seeker
p1/esc786:3.text: He's all of a sudden got an opinion on everything and tries to pull me into arguments with other friends.

p1/esc786:4.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:4.text: It sounds like he didn't use to blast his opinion in the past or include you in arguments, is that true?

p1/esc786:5.speaker: seeker
p1/esc786:5.text: That is true yes. It's like the world has to listen to his opinion and only his matters and he won't listen to reason. It's very frustrating and it makes me not want to talk to him. My eyes literally roll when I see a post from him.

p1/esc786:6.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:6.text: Oh I see! I get where you are coming from. I have a few friends that no matter how long you discuss, they won't let the conversation end unless "they are right." It seems like your friend doesn't like it when he is wrong?

p1/esc786:7.speaker: seeker
p1/esc786:7.text: Absolutely and I'm not sure how to broach this with him. I actually feel like it is damaging his reputation. Other friends of ours feel the same way. Not sure what to do?

p1/esc786:8.speaker: supporter
p1/esc786:8.text: Gotcha so not only are you frustrated with what he is doing, but you are also worried about his reputation! First of all, can I ask if he is just your friend online or if you hangout with him in person too?

p1/esc786:9.speaker: seeker
p1/esc786:9.text: That's correct. He is actually a close friend and I wonder what has changed recently to make him like this. I've known him for over 20 years.

p1/p1_conv_1:0.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_1:0.text: Hey, I hope you don't mind me reaching out.

p1/p1_conv_1:1.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_1:1.text: Not at all, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?

p1/p1_conv_1:10.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_1:10.text: Yeah, I guess I was worried people would think I'm overreacting.

p1/p1_conv_1:11.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_1:11.text: Your feelings are completely valid. Workplace harassment is serious, and it’s important to take it seriously.

p1/p1_conv_1:12.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_1:12.text: Thank you. I keep replaying moments in my head, wondering if I should have done something different.

p1/p1_conv_1:13.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_1:13.text: It's natural to question past actions, but it’s important to be kind to yourself. You're doing the best you can.

p1/p1_conv_1:14.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_1:14.text: I really appreciate that. I guess I need to figure out my next steps.

p1/p1_conv_1:15.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_1:15.text: Absolutely. Have you thought about what feels right for you moving forward? Maybe speaking to HR or a trusted colleague?

p1/p1_conv_1:16.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_1:16.text: I’ve thought about going to HR, but I’m scared about the repercussions.

p1/p1_conv_1:17.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_1:17.text: That’s understandable, and your concerns are valid. Is there someone at work you trust who could support you with this?

p1/p1_conv_1:18.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_1:18.text: There might be a couple of people, but I'm not sure if they'd want to get involved.

p1/p1_conv_1:19.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_1:19.text: Perhaps starting a conversation with them could help gauge their willingness to support you. It could be comforting not to face this alone.

p1/p1_conv_1:2.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_1:2.text: I had a bit of a breakdown at work recently. It was just... a lot.

p1/p1_conv_1:20.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_1:20.text: That’s a good idea. I’ll think about who I can talk to. It helps to know that it’s not hopeless.

p1/p1_conv_1:21.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_1:21.text: It's definitely not hopeless. You have options and I'm here to help you explore them. You’re not alone in this.

p1/p1_conv_1:22.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_1:22.text: Thank you so much. I feel a bit lighter after talking it through.

p1/p1_conv_1:23.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_1:23.text: I'm really glad to hear that. Remember, I'm just a message away if you need to talk again.

p1/p1_conv_1:3.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_1:3.text: I'm really sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what happened?

p1/p1_conv_1:4.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_1:4.text: Yeah, I just couldn't hold it together anymore. There's been this constant harassment, but I haven’t addressed it.

p1/p1_conv_1:5.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_1:5.text: That sounds incredibly tough and unfair. Thank you for trusting me with this. How long has this been going on?

p1/p1_conv_1:6.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_1:6.text: It's been months, maybe longer. I think I ignored it at first because I thought it would stop.

p1/p1_conv_1:7.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_1:7.text: I can understand hoping it would go away. It’s not easy to confront such issues. How does it make you feel to talk about it now?

p1/p1_conv_1:8.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_1:8.text: Honestly, it's a mix of relief and fear. Relief to finally say it out loud, but fear of what comes next.

p1/p1_conv_1:9.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_1:9.text: Those feelings make a lot of sense. It can be scary to think about the next steps, but voicing it is a strong first step.

p1/p1_conv_2:0.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_2:0.text: Hey there, thanks for being here today.

p1/p1_conv_2:1.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_2:1.text: Hi Sarah! I'm here to listen. How have you been doing lately?

p1/p1_conv_2:10.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_2:10.text: And the whole thing with my ex didn't help. I felt so betrayed and just... lost.

p1/p1_conv_2:11.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_2:11.text: It’s heartbreaking to go through betrayal like that. Your feelings are completely valid, and it's okay to feel lost.

p1/p1_conv_2:12.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_2:12.text: Thank you. I feel like I'm just venting but it's nice to have someone listen.

p1/p1_conv_2:13.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_2:13.text: I'm here to listen anytime you need. You're going through a lot, and it's important to let those feelings out.

p1/p1_conv_2:14.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_2:14.text: I’ve also been worried about my co-worker. The way our boss behaved with her... she seems uneasy, and I wish I could do more.

p1/p1_conv_2:15.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_2:15.text: It speaks volumes about your compassion that you’re concerned for her, too. Have you had a chance to talk with her about it?

p1/p1_conv_2:16.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_2:16.text: Not really. I don't want to overstep, but I also want her to know she's not alone.

p1/p1_conv_2:17.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_2:17.text: That's really thoughtful. Maybe just letting her know you're there if she needs someone to talk to could mean a lot.

p1/p1_conv_2:18.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_2:18.text: I'll try that. It's reassuring to hear I’m not overreacting.

p1/p1_conv_2:19.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_2:19.text: You're not overreacting at all. These are significant issues, and your feelings about them matter.

p1/p1_conv_2:2.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_2:2.text: It's been tough. I started therapy recently, and it's brought up a lot of emotions.

p1/p1_conv_2:20.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_2:20.text: I have to keep reminding myself that it's okay to speak up, even if it's hard.

p1/p1_conv_2:21.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_2:21.text: Absolutely. Your voice is important. And it’s okay to take small steps. You’re doing a lot just by starting to talk about it.

p1/p1_conv_2:22.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_2:22.text: Thanks for reminding me. I don't feel so alone knowing I have support.

p1/p1_conv_2:23.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_2:23.text: You’re never alone in this. Whenever you need to share or need reassurance, I’m here.

p1/p1_conv_2:3.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_2:3.text: Starting therapy can be a big step. It’s completely normal for it to stir up feelings. Do you want to share what's been coming up for you?

p1/p1_conv_2:4.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_2:4.text: Yeah, I guess. The breakup and everything at work...it just feels like too much sometimes.

p1/p1_conv_2:5.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_2:5.text: It sounds like you're carrying a lot right now. It's understandable to feel overwhelmed with everything you've been through.

p1/p1_conv_2:6.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_2:6.text: I agreed to therapy thinking it would help, but facing everything head-on is scarier than I thought.

p1/p1_conv_2:7.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_2:7.text: I can imagine how that might feel daunting. But it’s also courageous. It's the beginning of healing, even if it feels hard right now.

p1/p1_conv_2:8.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_2:8.text: I keep thinking about the harassment at work. Ignoring it for so long just made me feel so powerless.

p1/p1_conv_2:9.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_2:9.text: That must be incredibly difficult to deal with. It’s not easy to confront such issues, especially in a work environment.

p1/p1_conv_3:0.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:0.text: Hey, can I talk to you about something that's been on my mind?

p1/p1_conv_3:1.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_3:1.text: Of course, Sarah. What's been happening?

p1/p1_conv_3:10.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:10.text: That makes sense. I guess I'm just scared of making things worse, you know?

p1/p1_conv_3:11.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_3:11.text: That’s a common fear, but being there for your friend and offering a listening ear can do a lot of good. Have you noticed any changes in how you both interact since you found out?

p1/p1_conv_3:12.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:12.text: I’m trying to be more present when we're together. I feel like they've become more withdrawn, and it hurts to see.

p1/p1_conv_3:13.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_3:13.text: It's tough seeing someone you care about in pain. But showing up and letting them know they're not alone is supportive.

p1/p1_conv_3:14.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:14.text: I’ll keep that in mind. I just wish there was more I could do.

p1/p1_conv_3:15.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_3:15.text: Your friend is lucky to have someone as caring as you. When you're ready, maybe suggesting they talk to a professional could help.

p1/p1_conv_3:16.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:16.text: That’s a good point. Maybe I'll bring it up gently if the time feels right. It just feels like there’s so much to balance between work, therapy, and now worrying about my friend.

p1/p1_conv_3:17.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_3:17.text: It's a lot to juggle, for sure. Remember, you're not alone in this. How has work been since you started therapy?

p1/p1_conv_3:18.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:18.text: It's gotten better, slowly. I’m trying to set boundaries and leave work at the office.

p1/p1_conv_3:19.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_3:19.text: That sounds like progress. It's so important to set boundaries for your well-being. Do you feel therapy has helped you in that regard?

p1/p1_conv_3:2.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:2.text: I found out recently that my close friend has been dealing with depression, and it's really worrying me.

p1/p1_conv_3:20.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:20.text: Definitely. Having someone to talk to about these things has been grounding. I just need to remind myself to practice what I'm learning.

p1/p1_conv_3:21.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_3:21.text: It's wonderful to hear therapy is helping. Implementing what you’ve learned can take time, so be patient with yourself.

p1/p1_conv_3:22.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:22.text: Thanks. I’ll try to be kinder to myself. I really appreciate you listening and offering advice.

p1/p1_conv_3:23.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_3:23.text: Anytime, Sarah. Remember, you're doing your best, and that counts for a lot. Don't hesitate to reach out again if you need to talk.

p1/p1_conv_3:24.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:24.text: Thanks again. I’ll definitely reach out. Take care.

p1/p1_conv_3:3.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_3:3.text: I'm sorry to hear that. It must be difficult to know someone you care about is struggling. How are you handling it?

p1/p1_conv_3:4.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:4.text: Honestly, I'm feeling pretty overwhelmed. I want to help but I'm not sure how.

p1/p1_conv_3:5.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_3:5.text: Wanting to support your friend shows how much you care. It's okay not to have all the answers. Have you been able to talk to them about it?

p1/p1_conv_3:6.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:6.text: We talked a little. They admitted things have been tough but didn’t go into much detail. I don’t want to push them.

p1/p1_conv_3:7.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_3:7.text: It's great that they opened up to you a bit. Listening can be very supportive too. Have you been able to share some of what you're feeling with your therapist?

p1/p1_conv_3:8.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_3:8.text: Yeah, I mentioned it in therapy, but I feel guilty for focusing on my own feelings when my friend is the one struggling.

p1/p1_conv_3:9.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_3:9.text: Your feelings are valid too, Sarah. It’s natural to feel for your friend, but taking care of yourself is important. It helps you to be there for them.

p1/p1_conv_4:0.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_4:0.text: Hey, I hope you're available to chat for a bit. I could use some support right now.

p1/p1_conv_4:1.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_4:1.text: Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's been going on?

p1/p1_conv_4:10.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_4:10.text: Therapy has been really helpful. It's taught me ways to set boundaries and be more open about my feelings. I think it’s why I felt ready to approach my colleague.

p1/p1_conv_4:11.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_4:11.text: That's wonderful to hear. Taking those steps for personal growth can really make a difference. Have you talked to your therapist about starting this new relationship?

p1/p1_conv_4:12.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_4:12.text: Not yet, but I'm planning on bringing it up in my next session. My therapist has really helped me gain perspective on my relationships.

p1/p1_conv_4:13.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_4:13.text: That sounds like a great idea. Having professional guidance can really clarify things. How are things on the friendship front with your close friend?

p1/p1_conv_4:14.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_4:14.text: My friend is still struggling, which has been hard to watch. I've been trying to be there for them without overstepping.

p1/p1_conv_4:15.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_4:15.text: It must be tough to see someone you care about go through a hard time. How are you handling being supportive without taking on too much yourself?

p1/p1_conv_4:16.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_4:16.text: I try to listen and offer support when I can but also remind myself that their journey is separate from mine, and I need to set limits for my own well-being.

p1/p1_conv_4:17.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_4:17.text: That's a healthy approach. Remember, you can only do so much, and caring for yourself is crucial. How do you unwind after emotionally exhausting days?

p1/p1_conv_4:18.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_4:18.text: I've been getting into yoga and reading a lot lately. It helps me center myself and escape my thoughts for a while.

p1/p1_conv_4:2.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_4:2.text: Well, I finally told my colleague that I have feelings for him, and we decided to start dating.

p1/p1_conv_4:3.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_4:3.text: That's a big step! How are you feeling about it?

p1/p1_conv_4:4.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_4:4.text: I'm feeling a mix of excitement and worry. It's great to be with someone I connect with, but I'm also scared about how things might change at work.

p1/p1_conv_4:5.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_4:5.text: It's understandable to have those mixed feelings. Entering a new relationship is exciting but can also bring changes. What's your biggest concern right now?

p1/p1_conv_4:6.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_4:6.text: I guess I'm worried about how our colleagues might react. We both agreed to keep things professional, but gossip can be brutal.

p1/p1_conv_4:7.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_4:7.text: Office dynamics can be tricky. It sounds like you two have a good plan in place to stay professional. Do you think there's someone in the office you can confide in if things get challenging?

p1/p1_conv_4:8.speaker: seeker
p1/p1_conv_4:8.text: I do have a couple of colleagues who I trust. It's just that my last breakdown at work left me feeling a bit vulnerable. I'm trying to avoid that happening again.

p1/p1_conv_4:9.speaker: supporter
p1/p1_conv_4:9.text: It's great you have people you trust. And remember, you’ve come a long way since that incident. How have you been managing stress since starting therapy?

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: We were together almost ten years. Over nine and a half. I had no idea. I don't think the guy is even someone he really cares about. I don't know.

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: That's correct. He is actually a close friend and I wonder what has changed recently to make him like this. I've known him for over 20 years.

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: It's been months, maybe longer. I think I ignored it at first because I thought it would stop.

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: Just from home. Self-published author, some online work, stuff like that. He made about as much as I did, I wasn't the sole breadwinner or anything.

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: I agreed to therapy thinking it would help, but facing everything head-on is scarier than I thought.

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: Thanks for reminding me. I don't feel so alone knowing I have support.

spans.speaker: seeker

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: Not really. I don't want to overstep, but I also want her to know she's not alone.
